phase3_findings.description: No test calls verify_base_tables(..., dialect="sqlite") to assert RlsError with no cursor query (criterion 9); SQLite RLS tests were deleted and the refusal is only tested via dialect="postgres".

Criterion 9 has no test using the sqlite dialect for verify_base_tables; the unknown-dialect refusal is tested only with dialect="postgres" after the SQLite RLS tests were deleted. Runtime behavior is correct.
whole_row.py module docstring: 'is a catalog too' refers back to the removed sqlite_ sentence; uneven line wrap.

report:
## Verdict: REJECT (one Important test-coverage finding, raised by two agents)
The PR is not ready to merge: the code works, but the diff deletes every RLS test that ran under the `sqlite` dialect and adds no test that `verify_base_tables(..., dialect="sqlite")` is refused.
Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major
1. `tests/unit/test_rls_views.py` (lines 175-191): no test calls `verify_base_tables(connection, "SELECT a FROM t", dialect="sqlite")` and asserts `RlsError` with no `cursor.execute` call. The diff deleted the SQLite RLS tests (`test_sqlite_runs_no_routine_lookup` and others). The unknown-dialect refusal is now tested only with `dialect="postgres"`. The runtime behavior is correct: `src/sqllens/safety/relations.py` refuses the dialect before any query. Acceptance criterion 9 names this exact call. (raised by 2/5 agents)

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (1)
<details><summary>1 item</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/safety/whole_row.py` (lines 48-50): the module docstring says a credentials catalog such as `mysql.user` "is a catalog too". The word "too" pointed back to the removed `sqlite_` sentence and now refers to nothing. The line wrap is also uneven. (raised by 1/5 agents)

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred
- VC-15: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The Dockerfile comment says ChromaDB's store uses the stdlib sqlite3 module, so no database client library is installed. [docker/Dockerfile]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The Dockerfile comment (docker/Dockerfile:40-41) is authored text and chromadb is a declared dependency (pyproject.toml:35 chromadb>=0.5,<2; requirements.txt:31 chromadb==1.5.9). The item supplies no dependency_sources and chromadb source is not in head_view (no vendored copy; Grep of the view found only declarations). Whether chromadb's db/impl/sqlite code imports stdlib sqlite3 therefore cannot be settled from the views alone. Missing evidence: chromadb 1.5.9 source (chromadb/db/impl/sqlite.py) in a supplied dependency_sources directory.

  </details>

- VC-48: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The demo user can read the Chinook database and nothing else [examples/mysql-demo/demo-user.sql]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  examples/mysql-demo/demo-user.sql:3-4 creates chinook_reader@'%' and grants only SELECT ON `Chinook`.* (no global, other-schema, write or GRANT OPTION privileges), which supports the claim for user data schemas. The absolute wording 'nothing else' cannot be fully settled from the repository: MySQL server defaults (not in the repo) let any user read information_schema metadata (e.g. CHARACTER_SETS, COLLATIONS, ENGINES) and possibly some performance_schema variable/status tables without grants. I did not run the server to confirm which are readable, and no repository rule requires a stricter property; such reads expose server metadata, not other users' data.

  </details>

- VC-49: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The official mysql image runs files in /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d in file-name order, only when the data directory is empty, so 01-chinook.sql runs before 02-demo-user.sql [examples/mysql-demo/compose.yaml]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  compose.yaml:11-15 mounts Chinook_MySql.sql as /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/01-chinook.sql and demo-user.sql as 02-demo-user.sql, with the comment 'Scripts run once, in file-name order, when the data volume is empty.' The mount names sort correctly, so the claim holds if the image behaves as described. The claim concerns the mysql:8.0 image's docker-entrypoint.sh (docker_process_init_files and the DATABASE_ALREADY_EXISTS check), and that script is not in the views or under any supplied dependency_sources directory, so I could not read it. I did not run the image. The image behavior needs checking with `docker run --rm mysql:8.0 cat /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh`.

  </details>

- VC-57: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — The DatabaseConfig.dialect property still returns the scheme with +driver stripped, and callers needing a sqlglot dialect get 'mysql' for every accepted URL [src/sqllens/config.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  FAIL stored INCONCLUSIVE (requirement quote is missing): config.py:112-119 validator lowercases the scheme only for the check, so 'MySQL://u@h/db' or 'MYSQL+pymysql://...' is accepted, but returns the original value. config.py:127-128 dialect property does not lowercase: returns 'MySQL'/'MYSQL', not 'mysql'. The only remaining .dialect caller, eval/runner.py:295, passes it to compare_sql -> normalize_sql -> sqlglot Dialect.get_or_raise; sqlglot (.venv sqlglot/dialects/dialect.py:299-303, 1138-1142, _try_load 243) looks keys up case-sensitively, so 'MySQL' is unknown and raises, which compare_sql lets propagate (eval/compare.py:61). So not every accepted URL yields 'mysql' from .dialect. The other sqlglot-dialect callers (factory.py:117, query_database.py:874) use sqlglot_dialect_for_url (readonly.py:176-187), which lowercases and does return 'mysql' for every accepted URL. No 'sqlite' comparisons remain in src. The +driver stripping part holds.

  </details>

- VC-61: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — sqlglot exp.Table.db returns the schema qualifier string (empty for unqualified tables and table-valued functions) under the mysql dialect, so a table-valued function in FROM is never classified as a catalog. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:273]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  No dependency_sources were supplied and sqlglot source is not in the head view; Glob for sqlglot*/expressions* and site-packages/sqlglot/expressions* under /home/waran/Projects/R-LLC/sqllens found nothing. src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:273 uses (table.db or '').lower() in _catalog_names(dialect), whose correctness depends on sqlglot exp.Table.db behavior under mysql, which could not be read or run.

  </details>

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

I did not read any installed pymysql from the working tree or other venvs, as the rules forbid that. Missing evidence: pymysql/connections.py (Connection.connect) and CPython socket.create_connection, to confirm that no C-level connect bypasses the Python-level socket.socket.connect.

  </details>

- VC-75: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — Comment states MySQL returns a quoted alias label (with spaces/padding) exactly as written [tests/unit/test_safety_masking.py:248]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Client side verified: sql_runner.py:167-171 uses SSDictCursor and rows_to_capped_df (src/sqllens/safety/limits.py:62-69) builds pd.DataFrame([dict(row)...]) with no stripping or renaming, so whatever label the server sends survives verbatim. The comment (tests/unit/test_safety_masking.py:247-248) also claims MySQL server returns a quoted alias with trailing space exactly as written; that is server behavior (column-alias metadata handling of trailing spaces) which cannot be settled by reading repo source, and no PyMySQL/MySQL server source or run was available. Command not run: SELECT 1 AS `token_count ` against a MySQL server and inspect cursor.description.

  </details>

- VC-94: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — With `SQLLENS_LLM__API_KEY` set: 1. Start the demo container with `docker compose` from a fresh checkout and wait until it is ready. 2. Per the criterion, a run that cannot use Docker ends Blocked. I did not read criteria.json in full (matching lines were omitted as too long), so graded the criterion on its own text.

- VC-96: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — `LICENSES/THIRD-PARTY.txt` has a section for `examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql`. The section names the upstream project, the v1.4.5 release and its URL, and it carries the upstream copyright line and permission notice verbatim. [LICENSES/THIRD-PARTY.txt]

It names the Chinook Database (https://github.com/lerocha/chinook-database), release v1.4.5 and the URL https://github.com/lerocha/chinook-database/releases/tag/v1.4.5. The repository holds no copy of upstream LICENSE.md. The SQL header (Chinook_MySql.sql:8) only links to it. I had no network access to fetch it. My recollection is that upstream's copyright line may read '2008-2017', not '2008-2024', but I cannot confirm that. Missing evidence: upstream https://github.com/lerocha/chinook-database/blob/v1.4.5/LICENSE.md, to compare the copyright line and the permission notice byte for byte.

checklist.claim: The Dockerfile comment says ChromaDB's store uses the stdlib sqlite3 module, so no database client library is installed.
checklist.source_excerpt:
# The MySQL driver (PyMySQL) is pure Python, and ChromaDB's store uses the
# stdlib sqlite3 module, so no database client library is installed.
checklist.verify_against: chromadb package in the declared dependencies
checklist.verify_hint: Check chromadb's SQLite storage module (its `db/impl/sqlite` code) imports stdlib `sqlite3`
checklist.evidence: The Dockerfile comment (docker/Dockerfile:40-41) is authored text and chromadb is a declared dependency (pyproject.toml:35 chromadb>=0.5,<2; requirements.txt:31 chromadb==1.5.9). The item supplies no dependency_sources and chromadb source is not in head_view (no vendored copy; Grep of the view found only declarations). Whether chromadb's db/impl/sqlite code imports stdlib sqlite3 therefore cannot be settled from the views alone. Missing evidence: chromadb 1.5.9 source (chromadb/db/impl/sqlite.py) in a supplied dependency_sources directory.

checklist.claim: The demo user can read the Chinook database and nothing else
checklist.source_excerpt: -- Demo-only credentials: the user can read the Chinook database and nothing else.
checklist.verify_against: examples/mysql-demo/demo-user.sql grants and MySQL default privileges
checklist.verify_hint: Trace a SELECT by chinook_reader on information_schema or performance_schema tables, which MySQL lets any user read without a grant
checklist.evidence: examples/mysql-demo/demo-user.sql:3-4 creates chinook_reader@'%' and grants only SELECT ON `Chinook`.* (no global, other-schema, write or GRANT OPTION privileges), which supports the claim for user data schemas. The absolute wording 'nothing else' cannot be fully settled from the repository: MySQL server defaults (not in the repo) let any user read information_schema metadata (e.g. CHARACTER_SETS, COLLATIONS, ENGINES) and possibly some performance_schema variable/status tables without grants. I did not run the server to confirm which are readable, and no repository rule requires a stricter property; such reads expose server metadata, not other users' data.

checklist.evidence: FAIL stored INCONCLUSIVE (requirement quote is missing): config.py:112-119 validator lowercases the scheme only for the check, so 'MySQL://u@h/db' or 'MYSQL+pymysql://...' is accepted, but returns the original value. config.py:127-128 dialect property does not lowercase: returns 'MySQL'/'MYSQL', not 'mysql'. The only remaining .dialect caller, eval/runner.py:295, passes it to compare_sql -> normalize_sql -> sqlglot Dialect.get_or_raise; sqlglot (.venv sqlglot/dialects/dialect.py:299-303, 1138-1142, _try_load 243) looks keys up case-sensitively, so 'MySQL' is unknown and raises, which compare_sql lets propagate (eval/compare.py:61).
